summary.en: The big numbers in the news, and what they mean for your business.
summary.bs: Veliki brojevi iz vijesti i šta znače za tvoj biznis.

en.one: GDP is the total value of everything a country produces in a year. It is the size of the economy.
en.explain: It adds up the value of all final goods and services made inside the country: cars, haircuts, apartments, software. GDP growth shows whether the economy is expanding. GDP per person is often used to compare living standards.
en.example: If a country's GDP grows from €30 billion to €31.5 billion in a year, the economy grew 5%. After inflation, real growth may be smaller.
en.why: A growing economy usually means more customers with money to spend; a shrinking one means tougher sales.
en.mixup: GDP is not happiness or wealth. It does not count unpaid work, pollution or how fairly income is shared.

bs.one: GDP (BDP, bruto domaći proizvod) je ukupna vrijednost svega što država proizvede u godini. To je veličina ekonomije.
bs.explain: Sabere vrijednost svih krajnjih proizvoda i usluga napravljenih u zemlji: auta, šišanja, stanova, softvera. Rast BDP-a pokazuje da li se ekonomija širi. BDP po stanovniku se često koristi za poređenje životnog standarda.
bs.example: Ako BDP države naraste s 30 na 31,5 milijardi € za godinu, ekonomija je narasla 5%. Nakon inflacije stvarni rast može biti manji.
bs.why: Ekonomija koja raste obično znači više kupaca s novcem za trošenje; ona koja se smanjuje znači težu prodaju.
bs.mixup: BDP nije sreća ni bogatstvo. Ne broji neplaćeni rad, zagađenje ni koliko je pravedno raspodijeljen dohodak.

concepts.youtubeQuery: what is a recession explained simply

en.one: A recession is a period when the economy shrinks instead of growing, usually for at least two quarters in a row.
en.explain: People and firms spend less, sales fall, companies cut jobs and investment, and unemployment rises. Recessions can come from financial crises, sudden shocks like a pandemic, or high interest rates. They usually last months, not years.
en.example: During 2020, many countries' GDP fell sharply as shops closed. Restaurants lost most of their sales for months.
en.why: Businesses with cash reserves and flexible costs survive recessions; those with heavy debt and fixed costs often do not.
en.mixup: A recession is not the end of the economy. Many strong companies were started or grew during recessions.

bs.one: Recession (recesija) je period kad se ekonomija smanjuje umjesto da raste, obično najmanje dva kvartala zaredom.
bs.explain: Ljudi i firme troše manje, prodaja pada, firme smanjuju broj radnika i ulaganja, a nezaposlenost raste. Recesije mogu doći od finansijskih kriza, iznenadnih šokova kao pandemija ili visokih kamata. Obično traju mjesecima, ne godinama.
bs.example: Tokom 2020. BDP mnogih zemalja je naglo pao jer su radnje zatvorene. Restorani su mjesecima izgubili većinu prodaje.
bs.why: Firme s rezervama novca i fleksibilnim troškovima prežive recesije; one s velikim dugom i fiksnim troškovima često ne.
bs.mixup: Recesija nije kraj ekonomije. Mnoge jake firme su pokrenute ili narasle tokom recesija.

en.one: The unemployment rate is the share of people who want a job and are looking, but do not have one.
en.explain: It does not count students, retirees or people not looking for work. High unemployment means weak demand and easier hiring; low unemployment means people have money to spend but workers are harder to find and wages rise.
en.example: If 100,000 people are in the labour force and 8,000 are looking for work, the unemployment rate is 8%.
en.why: It tells you how easy it will be to hire, and how much customers might spend.
en.mixup: Low unemployment is not always easy for business. It often means a fight for staff and rising wage costs.

bs.one: Unemployment rate (stopa nezaposlenosti) je udio ljudi koji žele posao i traže ga, a nemaju ga.
bs.explain: Ne broji studente, penzionere ni ljude koji ne traže posao. Visoka nezaposlenost znači slabu potražnju i lakše zapošljavanje; niska znači da ljudi imaju novca za trošenje, ali je radnike teže naći i plate rastu.
bs.example: Ako je 100.000 ljudi u radnoj snazi, a 8.000 traži posao, stopa nezaposlenosti je 8%.
bs.why: Govori ti koliko će biti lako zaposliti i koliko bi kupci mogli trošiti.
bs.mixup: Niska nezaposlenost nije uvijek laka za firme. Često znači borbu za radnike i rast troškova plata.

en.one: The business cycle is the repeating rise and fall of the economy: growth, peak, slowdown, low point, recovery.
en.explain: Economies do not grow in a straight line. Good times bring more spending and borrowing until things overheat; then spending falls until the economy recovers again. The length of each phase varies.
en.example: Construction booms when credit is cheap and the economy grows, then slows sharply when rates rise and buyers pull back.
en.why: Planning for the down phase while times are good is what keeps a business alive through the whole cycle.
en.mixup: Nobody can predict the exact timing of the next turn. Plan for it, but do not bet everything on guessing it.

bs.one: Business cycle (privredni ciklus) je ponavljajući rast i pad ekonomije: rast, vrhunac, usporavanje, dno, oporavak.
bs.explain: Ekonomije ne rastu pravolinijski. Dobra vremena donose više trošenja i zaduživanja dok se stvari ne pregriju; onda trošenje pada dok se ekonomija opet ne oporavi. Dužina svake faze varira.
bs.example: Građevina cvjeta kad su krediti jeftini i ekonomija raste, a onda naglo uspori kad kamate porastu i kupci se povuku.
bs.why: Planiranje za lošu fazu dok su vremena dobra je ono što firmu drži živom kroz cijeli ciklus.
bs.mixup: Niko ne može predvidjeti tačno vrijeme sljedećeg preokreta. Planiraj za njega, ali ne kladi se sve na pogađanje.

en.one: Productivity is how much output you get from each hour of work or each euro of input.
en.explain: Better tools, skills, processes and technology let people produce more in the same time. Over the long run, rising productivity is the main reason wages and living standards rise.
en.example: A bookkeeper using good software processes 400 invoices a day instead of 150. Same hours, more output.
en.why: Higher productivity lets you pay better wages and still keep prices competitive.
en.mixup: Productivity is not working longer hours. It is getting more done in the same hours.

bs.one: Productivity (produktivnost) je koliko rezultata dobiješ iz svakog sata rada ili svakog eura ulaganja.
bs.explain: Bolji alati, vještine, procesi i tehnologija omogućavaju ljudima da proizvedu više u istom vremenu. Dugoročno, rast produktivnosti je glavni razlog zašto rastu plate i životni standard.
bs.example: Knjigovođa s dobrim softverom obradi 400 faktura dnevno umjesto 150. Isti sati, više rezultata.
bs.why: Veća produktivnost ti omogućava da plaćaš bolje plate, a da cijene ostanu konkurentne.
bs.mixup: Produktivnost nije duži rad. To je postići više u istim satima.

concepts.youtubeQuery: consumer price index CPI explained simply

en.one: The CPI tracks the price of a typical 'shopping basket' over time. Its yearly change is the official inflation rate.
en.explain: Statisticians check the prices of hundreds of everyday things like food, rent, fuel, clothes and services each month. If the basket costs 4% more than a year ago, inflation is 4%.
en.example: Last year the basket cost €1,000; now it costs €1,035. Inflation is 3.5%.
en.why: Contracts, wages, rents and pensions are often adjusted by CPI, so it directly affects your costs.
en.mixup: Your own costs may rise faster or slower than the CPI. A café feels coffee and energy prices more than the average basket.

bs.one: CPI (indeks potrošačkih cijena) prati cijenu tipične 'potrošačke korpe' kroz vrijeme. Njegova godišnja promjena je zvanična stopa inflacije.
bs.explain: Statističari svaki mjesec provjeravaju cijene stotina svakodnevnih stvari kao što su hrana, kirija, gorivo, odjeća i usluge. Ako korpa košta 4% više nego prije godinu, inflacija je 4%.
bs.example: Prošle godine korpa je koštala 1.000 €; sada košta 1.035 €. Inflacija je 3,5%.
bs.why: Ugovori, plate, kirije i penzije se često usklađuju po CPI, pa direktno utiče na tvoje troškove.
bs.mixup: Tvoji troškovi mogu rasti brže ili sporije od CPI. Kafić više osjeti cijene kafe i energije nego prosječna korpa.
